newsitem.title: UK: Brit Midland asks Commission to limit US slot handover.
newsitem.headline: Brit Midland asks Commission to limit US slot handover.

text.p: British Midland, the short-haul airline, is set to call on the European Commission to limit the number of landing slots that could be handed over to U.S. carriers under the conditions for clearing the British Airways and American Airlines' transatlantic alliance.
Sir Michael Bishop, chairman of British Midland, said it opposed more than 168 slots being given to U.S. airlines.
He said some reports suggested BA could be forced to release 500-600 landing slots at Heathrow and urged that these additional slots be shared out among European carriers, including BM.

Bishop told a London press briefing that its submission to the Commission this week would state that if more than 168 slots were given over to other U.S. airlines it would lead to Heathrow being dominated by already competitively priced transatlantic flights.

He said the European flight market, particularly in the business sector, could benefit from being awarded extra slots. He said there had been reports Commission officials were considering forcing BA to release up to 600 slots if it wanted the deal to go through.

"We are content with 168 slots (the current UK condition). But not with 500-600. It is quite disproportionate," he said, adding: "Let competition develop in Europe, rather than just the transatlantic market."

British Midland suggests that if BA is forced to release over 168 slots, BM should get an allocation of the additional amount in relation to its current share of Heathrow slots, which stands at 13 percent of the total.
